title: Mental Health Assessment Prototype — 100 Multiple-Choice Questions in Seven Domains
intendedUse: Educational / research prototype; NOT a clinically validated or deployable medical diagnostic tool.
importantSafetyAndMethodology: The initial 50 items are paraphrases of seven published instruments, and the 50 additional items are originally written for prototyping. NONE of the 100 items should be treated as a validated instrument version.

The named instruments have fixed item counts (for example, PHQ-9 has 9, GAD-7 has 7, and WHO-5 has 5). The new questions are optional, clearly labeled supplemental items, NOT extensions of those validated tools.
When computing a named instrument reference score, NEVER include supplemental_original items. Because the core items are paraphrased, even their reference scores are not clinically validated.
Published screening cutoffs are NOT automatically valid after item wording changes; all officialReferenceBands are disabled.
For a real clinical feature, replace paraphrases with authorized official instrument forms, preserve original response choices and recall periods, and obtain qualified clinician review.
Score each assessment independently. NEVER sum all 50 items as if they measured one disorder.
No questionnaire alone can confirm a psychiatric diagnosis. Show non-diagnostic screening results and appropriate next steps.
If any self-harm item is endorsed, activate a separately approved safety response irrespective of the total score.
Do not record identifying or sensitive health data unnecessarily; protect responses, enforce consent and access control.
Assessments should generally be user-selected; do not require a user to complete all 50 questions.
Verify licensing, especially for commercial use and translated versions. PSS-10 is intentionally excluded because the owner requests permission via MAPI ePROVIDE.

assessmentSelection.defaultResultHeading: Screening response summary — not a diagnosis
assessmentSelection.showSupplementalAs: Optional exploratory questions (not part of the validated named instrument)
assessmentSelection.scoringScope: For prototype summaries, use assessment.questionIds for the 50 core adapted items; use assessment.supplementalQuestionIds for custom exploratory questions. Keep both subtotals separate and do not apply clinical score bands.

PHQ9.reuse_note: Pfizer released PHQ and GAD scales without copyright restriction; the prompts in this file are nonetheless original paraphrases, not the validated official wording.
PHQ9.citation: Kroenke K, Spitzer RL, Williams JBW (2001). The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure. Journal of General Internal Medicine, 16, 606–613.

GAD7.reuse_note: The official scale is freely available; the prompts in this file are original paraphrases rather than the validated original wording.
GAD7.citation: Spitzer RL, Kroenke K, Williams JBW, Lowe B (2006). A brief measure for assessing generalized anxiety disorder: the GAD-7. Archives of Internal Medicine, 166, 1092–1097.

K6.reuse_note: Author allows use of the official K6 without formal permission, but requests attribution and copyright credit; wording here is paraphrased.
K6.citation: Kessler RC et al. (2003). Screening for serious mental illness in the general population. Archives of General Psychiatry, 60(2), 184–189. Copyright © Ronald C. Kessler, PhD. All rights reserved.

RSES.organization: Morris Rosenberg / University of Maryland Department of Sociology
RSES.reuse_note: University of Maryland states the original Rosenberg scale is public domain. This file uses original paraphrases and the 0-30 scoring orientation and item order of the UMD version.
RSES.citation: Rosenberg M (1965). Society and the Adolescent Self-Image. Princeton University Press.

WHO5.reuse_note: WHO 2024 source is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO: non-commercial share-alike with attribution, and commercial uses need permission. Prompts here are paraphrases; check whether adaptation terms apply before redistribution.
WHO5.citation: World Health Organization (2024). The World Health Organization-Five Well-Being Index (WHO-5). WHO/UCN/MSD/MHE/2024.1. CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO.

GSE.reuse_note: Source states permission for non-commercial research and development, including adaptations. Verify commercial deployment rights. Prompts here are paraphrased.
GSE.citation: Schwarzer R, Jerusalem M (1995). Generalized Self-Efficacy Scale. In: Weinman J, Wright S, Johnston M (eds), Measures in Health Psychology: A Users Portfolio.

UCLA3.organization: Hughes, Waite, Hawkley & Cacioppo; see UK Office for National Statistics
UCLA3.reuse_note: Prompts here are paraphrases; check re-use rights with the original scale rights holder before commercial deployment.
UCLA3.citation: Hughes ME, Waite LJ, Hawkley LC, Cacioppo JT (2004). A short scale for measuring loneliness in large surveys. Research on Aging, 26(6), 655–672.

questions.text: Have activities that normally interest you seemed less enjoyable than usual?
Have you spent a lot of time feeling unhappy or without hope?
Has your sleep been disrupted or much longer than usual?
Have you struggled with tiredness or too little energy for daily tasks?
Has your appetite changed substantially, whether eating less or more?
Have you judged yourself harshly or felt you had let people down?
Has staying focused on reading, studying, or watching something been difficult?
Have you moved or spoken unusually slowly, or felt noticeably more restless?
Have thoughts about ending your life or deliberately hurting yourself occurred?

safetyFlag.name: self_harm_thoughts
safetyFlag.instructions: Never wait for a total score to respond to this item; offer urgent local help when there is immediate danger. Have a clinician design and review the workflow.

Overall, I accept myself as a person.
I wish I valued and respected myself more.
I sometimes feel that I am not useful.
At times, I believe that I am not good enough.
I experienced a cheerful, positive mood.
I felt peaceful and at ease.
I had enough vitality to be active.
I woke up feeling restored after sleep.
My day-to-day life included things I found engaging.

I feel capable of handling a surprising change in circumstances.
When unexpected issues arise, I can usually figure out how to respond.

I feel prepared to deal with most ordinary challenges that come my way.
How often do you wish you had more companionship?
How often do you feel excluded from groups or social situations?
How often do you feel disconnected from other people?
Have you avoided starting everyday activities because it felt emotionally difficult to begin?

safetyRules.name: self_harm_question
safetyRules.note: This may be an urgent safety concern regardless of the other scores; crisis handling must be developed and tested with professionals.

resultDisplayGuidance.suggestedDisclaimer: These questions support a learning/prototype project and are not diagnostic. The original 50 prompts are paraphrased, and the additional 50 prompts are unvalidated custom questions. Their scores cannot determine whether you have any mental health condition. A qualified professional can provide an appropriate assessment.

supplementaryQuestionPolicy.numericOptionScores: For testing MCQ scoring in a student software project only; not validated measurements.
supplementaryQuestionPolicy.guidance: Original reference instruments and supplemental questions must be scored separately. If you want evidence-based clinical screening, replace adapted core items with authorized exact official items and keep their lengths, choices, and scoring intact; seek professional review.
